original_question:
For the modified focusing cubic NLS

 i P_2(epsilon nabla) partial_t v + Delta v + |v|^2 v = 0,

assume that the positive self-adjoint operator P_2(epsilon nabla) gives only partial off-axis regularization, meaning it controls derivatives only in some distinguished directions rather than the full H^1 norm. Can one develop both the local and the global well-posedness theory in that partial off-axis case, and in particular decide whether this partial off-axis dependence is enough to prevent finite-time breakdown of solutions that would blow up for the standard focusing cubic NLS?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 4 in §4.1.4, Off-Axis Variation of the Group Velocity, concerning Eq. (60) under the partial off-axis dependence hypothesis (66). ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant modification of the focusing cubic NLS through the operator P_2(ε∇), the key distinction between full and only directional off-axis control, the two analytic tasks the paper singles out (local and global well-posedness), and the main qualitative issue: whether this weaker anisotropic modification can prevent the finite-time breakdown present for the focusing cubic NLS. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s target is not the fully general model (3), but its specialization with α_2 = 0, α_3 = 0, and f = 0, which is Eq. (60). ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The ambient setting is v : [0,T) × R^d → C, with ε > 0 small and P_2(ε∇) assumed to be a second-order-at-most, self-adjoint, positive operator. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The scope is the no/anomalous GVD regime of §4.1, not the normal-GVD case of §4.2: specifically, d = 2 when α_1 = 0 and d = 3 when α_1 = 1. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The paper’s term is partial off-axis dependence, and it is defined quantitatively by (66), not just informally as partial regularization. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

Precisely, partial off-axis dependence means that there exist j < d linearly independent vectors v_k ∈ R^d such that (P_2(ε∇)v,v) >= ||v||_{L^2}^2 + ε^2 Σ_{k=1}^j ||v_k · ∇v||_{L^2}^2; the paper further specifies j = 1 if d = 2, and j = 1 or 2 if d = 3. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The nearby benchmark result you did not mention is that full off-axis dependence already gives H^1 local well-posedness and then global existence, using the conserved energy and the modified mass (61); Open Problem 4 asks whether an analogous theory survives under only partial off-axis control. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The conserved quantity replacing the usual mass is (P_2(ε∇)v(t),v(t)) = (P_2(ε∇)v_0,v_0), and this is part of the context for the hoped-for global theory. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The hidden analytic difficulty is anisotropic: P_2(ε∇)^(-1) gains two derivatives only along the regularized directions v_k, while the semigroup is expected to provide useful dispersion/Strichartz control only in the orthogonal directions. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

Your draft narrows the blow-up question to data that already blow up for the standard NLS, but Open Problem 4 is broader: it asks whether adding partial off-axis dependence prevents finite-time breakdown of solutions to Eq. (60) in general. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be tied specifically to Eq. (60) in §4.1.4, rather than to an arbitrary partially regularized focusing cubic NLS. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
refined_question: For the scalar modified NLS Eq. (60), i P_2(ε∇) ∂_t v + Δ v + |v|^2 v = 0 on R^d in the no/anomalous GVD setting of §4.1 (so d = 2 when α_1 = 0 and d = 3 when α_1 = 1), with α_2 = α_3 = 0, f = 0, ε > 0, v complex-valued, and P_2(ε∇) a second-order-at-most, self-adjoint, positive operator, assume only partial off-axis dependence in the precise sense that there exist linearly independent vectors v_k ∈ R^d, k = 1, ..., j, with j < d (j = 1 if d = 2; j = 1 or 2 if d = 3), such that (P_2(ε∇)v,v) >= ||v||_{L^2}^2 + ε^2 Σ_{k=1}^j ||v_k · ∇v||_{L^2}^2. Can one establish a local and global well-posedness theory for Eq. (60) in this partial off-axis regime and determine, in light of the conserved energy and the modified mass (P_2(ε∇)v(t),v(t)) = (P_2(ε∇)v_0,v_0), whether adding only this partial off-axis dependence prevents finite-time breakdown of solutions? ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because §4.1.4 first treats the full off-axis case, proves H^1 local and global well-posedness there, then isolates the partial off-axis condition (66) and immediately states Open Problem 4 asking exactly for local/global well-posedness and whether partial off-axis dependence prevents finite-time breakdown. The main correction to your draft is scope: the paper does not restrict the question to initial data already known to blow up for the standard cubic NLS, but asks the broader no-breakdown question for Eq. (60) itself in the partial off-axis regime. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
